text:
maya: Heads-up — we're getting a steady wave of small GPU pod evictions in asia-sg (ap-southeast1). Pods show Pending with `InsufficientGPU` while nodes report free fractional capacity.

maya: sample from `kubectl describe pod` — shows nodeAffinity to `gpu-type: h100` and toleration for `gpu-isolated:NoSchedule`. Pods are 1-GPU containers.

maya: ```
Events:
  Type    Reason         Age   From               Message
  ----    ------         ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient gpu, 18 node(s) had taint {gpu-isolated:NoSchedule}, 0 match node selector.
```

sam: cc @andre @jen  — did the taint rollout for GPU isolation hit asia-sg?

andre: not that rollout. I checked the node histories — a couple of NIC flaps triggered kubelet to mark nodes `gpu-isolated` during emergency drain cleanup last night. Those taints didn't get cleared when nodes rejoined.

jen: confirming — controlplane logs show `mark-node-unschedulable` ran as part of a spot reclaim-handler job around 03:12 UTC. Some of the nodes got re-labeled but the taint lingered.

opsbot: autoscaler: scaledown decided for asia-sg1: removed 12 preemptible nodes at 03:15 UTC (policy: aggressive).

liam: looks like two issues combining: (1) sticky taints from reclaim/drain, (2) strict nodeAffinity to `gpu-type: h100` + mixed GPU fleet. That creates packing holes: 1-GPU pods can't fit into H100 nodes when scheduler sees taints or mismatched labels.

maya: suggestion: conservative fix first — clear stale taint on nodes that passed health checks, then run a small descheduler/compact job to consolidate 1-GPU pods onto multi-GPU nodes, freeing up whole nodes for batch workloads.

sam: agree. We should be careful: compacting will force extra evictions which could cause user-visible latency. Need a canary window and a rollback plan.

andre: commands I'm going to run in a moment (canary, 2 nodes):
```bash
# remove stale taint from node(s) that are Ready
kubectl taint nodes node-asia-03 gpu-isolated:NoSchedule-
# run descheduler pod (policy: low-priority, max-evictions 10)
kubectl apply -f descheduler-canary.yaml
```

jen: descheduler policy suggestion: prefer evicting tiny pods < 2Gi memory and 1rps steady-state. Keep pods with long-lived KV caches pinned. I'll paste policy in channel.

maya: pasted the failing pod list to PagerDuty ticket PD-734. If this goes sideways, we have rollback: re-add taints and scale up warm pool.

liam: quick cost note: if we consolidate and hit spot reclaim we might see a spike in transient evictions — short-term SLO hits but better utilization -> lower monthly GPU cost. Flagging Finance/ops for visibility.

sam: +1 on canary. Also we need to relax nodeAffinity in our inference-service helm chart long-term. Hard pinning to `gpu-type: h100` is causing brittle packing when AZs have mixed instance classes.

andre: on it — I'll open a PR with a feature-flagged affinity relaxation (fallback to `gpu-family: ampere` if exact match not found).

jen: can someone run `kubectl get nodes -l gpu-type=h100 -o wide` and paste output? want to verify which nodes were tainted but Ready.

maya: pasted nodes: node-asia-02 (Ready, taint present), node-asia-07 (Ready, taint present). I'll remove taint on -02 now and watch scheduler behavior.

opsbot: event: taint removal performed by maya at 03:46 UTC on node-asia-02

sam: watching pods — a couple of Pending 1-GPU pods moved onto node-asia-02, scheduling latency ~12s. so far so good.

liam: :thumbsup: small follow-up — add an alert for stale gpu taints per region (runbook pointer: infra/runbooks/gpu-taint-cleanup).

maya: action items:
- liam: create alert + link to runbook (ETA 24h)
- andre: PR for affinity fallback (ETA: today EOD)
- jen: prepare descheduler policy and hold window (ETA: 1hr)
- maya: run canary taint clear + descheduler on 2 nodes now, monitor for 30m

sam: thanks all. ping here when the 30m window passes and we'll decide whether to roll to rest of nodes.

jen: on it, will post results in 30m.

liam: noted for finance FYI.

maya: done for canary, monitoring metrics — will update.

jen: 30m update: canary completed, evictions were ~8 (within expectation), scheduling backlog cleared, no regressions in latency. Recommend gradual rollout to remaining Ready nodes that have the stale taint.

sam: +1 — go ahead with gradual rollout during low traffic window. Thanks everyone. :heavy_check_mark:
